z-m-13-08.title: Test Gaon claim 'method only use when it divides evenly'
z-m-13-08.topic: Fraction division: range where common-denominator then numerator division works
z-m-13-08.goal: Use counterexample test claim method only works if numerators divide evenly; explain why method work every time.
z-m-13-08.material: When divide fractions, one method find common denominator then divide numerators. Example 4/5÷2/5 share denominator, so 4÷2=2. Gaon say, 'Only use common-denominator and divide-numerators method when numerator divides evenly. If no, don't use am.' (4/5 read four fifths; 2/5 two fifths.)
z-m-13-08.thinking.0: Judge what example fit break a claim
z-m-13-08.s.s1.prompt: Which example best test if Gaon statement right?
z-m-13-08.s.s1.hint.0: Rewrite in one sentence the case where Gaon say don't use method.

z-m-13-08.s.s1.r.a: Reciprocal method one you know already. It no test Gaon claim.
z-m-13-08.s.s1.o.b: Choose division wey no divide evenly and test whether common-denominator answer correct.
z-m-13-08.s.s1.o.c: Choose only divisions with same denominator and test method.
z-m-13-08.s.s1.r.c: Same-denominator fractions no need common denominator. Need cases wey actually require one.
z-m-13-08.s.s1.o.d: Collect more examples where numerator divides evenly and check method.
z-m-13-08.s.s1.r.d: Even more evenly-dividing examples no break claim 'only when divisible'. Claim concern cases wey no divide evenly.
z-m-13-08.s.s1.explain: Gaon claim say 'only use when e divide evenly'. If wrong, must be examples where common-denominator method still right when numerator no divide evenly. Find those examples and compare with reciprocal method result.
z-m-13-08.s.s2.prompt: Make 2 different divisions a/b÷c/d where after common denominator, numerators no divide evenly (remainder no be 0). Both fractions proper, irreducible and below 1; denominators at most 12 and different. Use least common multiple as common denominator.
z-m-13-08.s.s2.hint.0: First choose denominators and find LCM. Convert fractions to that denominator and get numerators.
z-m-13-08.s.s2.hint.1: Divide first numerator by second, check directly remainder no be 0; otherwise change fractions.
z-m-13-08.s.s2.ok.c1: Numerators and denominators na positive whole numbers.
z-m-13-08.s.s2.fail.c1: Make numerators at least 1 and denominators natural numbers no more than 12.
z-m-13-08.s.s2.ok.c2: Both fractions be reduced proper fractions less than 1.
z-m-13-08.s.s2.fail.c2: Both fractions must be reduced proper fractions below 1.
z-m-13-08.s.s2.fail.c3: Denominators same. Make dem different so common denominator needed.
z-m-13-08.s.s2.ok.c4: Numerators after finding common denominator no divide evenly.
z-m-13-08.s.s2.fail.c4: Numerators after common denominator divide evenly. Find common denominator and numerators, divide and switch to fractions with remainder.
z-m-13-08.s.s2.explain: For example, common denominator for 5/6÷1/3 give 5/6÷2/6; 5÷2 no divide evenly but equal 5/2. Same as 5/6×3=5/2 by reciprocal method. 2/3÷3/4 becomes 8/12÷9/12, so 8÷9=8/9, same as 2/3×4/3=8/9. Once denominator same, fraction quotient equal quotient of numerators; if division has remainder, write quotient as fraction.

z-m-13-08.s.s3.model.1: No matter say e no divide evenly, write quotient as fraction. 1/2÷3/4=2/4÷3/4, so 2÷3=2/3, same as 1/2×4/3=2/3.
z-m-13-08.s.s3.model.2: 1/2÷1/3=3/6÷2/6=3÷2. Even if no divide evenly, write quotient 3/2; this method still work.

z-m-13-06.title: If 5 people share 2 cakes, how many pieces each go get?

z-m-13-06.goal: Separate that whole-number division quotient fit write as fraction (an amount) from saying how many pieces (need more info about cutting); find cases divisible without leftovers and different solutions when not.
z-m-13-06.material: Somi group get 5 people and want share 2 same-size cakes equally. Each cake fit cut into equal pieces, but dem never decide piece count. Teacher ask 'How many pieces each person go eat?' Somi answer '2 ÷ 5 = 2/5 (two fifths), so na 2/5 of one piece.'

z-m-13-06.s.s1.o.a: Correct. 2÷5=2/5, each person eat 2/5 of a piece.
z-m-13-06.s.s1.r.a: 2/5 show amount of cake. Piece size depend on how dem cut, so we no fit say '2/5 of one piece'.

z-m-13-06.s.s1.r.d: Problem already tell us say 2 cakes dey. Check what information still missing.
z-m-13-06.s.s1.explain: 2÷5=2/5 mean each person get 2/5 of one cake. To say how many pieces, we need know how many pieces dem cut each cake into. If cake cut into 5, each get 2 pieces; if cut into 10, each get 4. Same 2/5 cake fit mean different piece counts depending on cutting.

z-m-13-01.title: 'She drink 2/5.' How many L be that?
z-m-13-01.topic: Fraction multiplication word problems: read whether fraction mean 'amount' or 'share of the whole'
z-m-13-01.goal: Notice say answer change depending whether fraction without unit mean 'that much amount' or 'part of the whole'; make examples yourself where the two readings differ plenty, and rewrite sentence so e fit only one way.
z-m-13-01.material: Sujin drink 2/5 (two fifths) of the 3/4 L (three-fourths liter) water wey dey inside bottle. Teacher ask, 'How many L water remain?' Eunu answer 3/4 − 2/5 = 7/20 L, and Harin answer 3/4 × 3/5 = 9/20 L. Both read same sentence and get different answers. (At first, bottle get only 3/4 L and nobody add water while she dey drink.)

z-m-13-01.s.s1.explain: No 'L' follow 2/5, so dem fit read am two ways. If she drink 2/5 L, then 3/4 − 2/5 = 7/20 L remain; if she drink 2/5 of original water, then 3/4 × (1 − 2/5) = 3/4 × 3/5 = 9/20 L remain. Eunu and Harin each choose one reading, and calculation correct within their own reading. To choose one answer, you need know wetin 2/5 mean.

z-m-13-01.s.s2.ok.c3: Even if you read am as 'she drink p/q L', e less than 3/4 L, so e make sense.
z-m-13-01.s.s2.fail.c3: If p/q na 3/4 or more, you no fit read am as 'she drink p/q L'. She no fit drink more than 3/4 L.

z-m-13-01.s.s2.fail.c4: Difference between remaining amounts for the two readings less than 1/10 L. Change fraction she drink, find both remaining amounts and compare the difference.

z-m-13-04.s.s2.fail.c2: Left: 3/4÷3/8=2, then 2×p/q=2p/q. Group back: 3/4÷(3/8×p/q)=2q/p. Equal only if p=q, i.e. p/q=1. Example 2/5 gives 4/5 versus 5.
z-m-13-04.s.s2.explain: For 3/4÷3/8×p/q, when do two calculation orders give equal values? Use at least one tested example and state guess. 3 4 3 8 2 2 2 3 4 3 8 2 1 2 5 4 5 5 3 4 3 8 2 2 2 3 4 3 8 2 1 2 5 4 5 5

z-m-13-04.s.s2.because.hint.0: Compare equal and different cases for common form.

z-m-13-07.thinking.1: Make examples wey meet the conditions
z-m-13-07.title: Raon calculation trick: how far e work?
z-m-13-07.topic: Decimal multiplication: see decimal multiplier as fraction and change multiplication to division
z-m-13-07.goal: Use decimal-fraction relationship explain why changing multiplication by decimal to division work, find decimals it works for, then test cases wey fail and set limits.
z-m-13-07.material: Raon calculate 7.2×0.25 like this: '0.25 na 1/4, so I fit just divide 7.2 by 4. 7.2÷4=1.8!' When calculate 7.2×0.25 normally, answer too na 1.8. Raon excited say, 'Any multiplication by decimal fit change to division this way!' (7.2 read seven point two; 0.25 read zero point two five.)
z-m-13-07.thinking.2: Test generalization and set its range
z-m-13-07.prereq.2: Connection between taking 1/4 of number and dividing by 4
z-m-13-07.s.s1.prompt: Why 7.2×0.25 calculated as 7.2÷4 give same answer?
z-m-13-07.s.s1.hint.1: 1/4 of 7.2 na one of how many equal parts of 7.2?
z-m-13-07.s.s1.o.a: Both calculations just happen to give same answer.
z-m-13-07.s.s1.r.a: Na no coincidence. Reason link multiplying 0.25 with dividing by 4.
z-m-13-07.s.s1.o.b: Division easier than multiplication, so this way okay.
z-m-13-07.s.s1.r.b: Easy method na reason to choose calculation, no be reason results equal.
z-m-13-07.s.s1.o.c: Because 0.25 has 2 decimal places, so you can divide by 4.
z-m-13-07.s.s1.r.c: No every number with 2 decimal places fit change to division by something. Need look at what kind number 0.25 be.
z-m-13-07.s.s1.o.d: 0.25=1/4, and multiply by 1/4 same as divide by 4.
z-m-13-07.s.s1.explain: 0.25=25/100=1/4. One-fourth of a number means one of 4 equal parts, so multiplying by 1/4 same as dividing by 4. 7.2×0.25=1.8 and 7.2÷4=1.8. [1, 4]
z-m-13-07.s.s2.prompt: Find decimals c wey Raon method (read multiplier as 1/k and divide by k) works. c > 0 and < 1, max 2 decimal places, 1/c natural number. Find 3 different c.
z-m-13-07.s.s2.hint.0: Write decimal multiplier as fraction and see if numerator become 1.
z-m-13-07.s.s2.hint.1: Write some decimals as fractions and group ones with numerator 1 and ones without.
z-m-13-07.s.s2.fail.c1: c must be above 0 and below 1.
z-m-13-07.s.s2.ok.c2: c has no more than 2 decimal places.
z-m-13-07.s.s2.fail.c2: Make c no more than 2 decimal places (like 0.25).
z-m-13-07.s.s2.fail.c3: 1/c no be natural number. Check if fraction form of c get numerator 1.
z-m-13-07.s.s2.explain: If c as fraction get numerator 1 (1/k), multiplying by am can turn to division by k. With up to 2 decimals: 0.5 (=1/2), 0.25 (=1/4), 0.2 (=1/5), 0.1 (=1/10), 0.05 (=1/20), 0.04 (=1/25), 0.02 (=1/50), 0.01 (=1/100).
z-m-13-07.s.s3.prompt: Raon say any decimal multiplication fit become division this way! Test multiplying 7.2 by 0.3 and write wetin you tell Raon.
z-m-13-07.s.s3.hint.0: Calculate 7.2×0.3 and 7.2÷3 and write results side by side.
z-m-13-07.s.s3.hint.1: Write 0.3 as fraction and compare with 0.25=1/4.
z-m-13-07.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You write both values (product and quotient)?
z-m-13-07.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You explain why 0.3 as fraction differ from dividing by 3?
z-m-13-07.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You also say which decimals Raon method works for?
z-m-13-07.s.s3.model.0: 7.2×0.3=2.16 but 7.2÷3=2.4, so different. 0.3 no be 1/3; e be 3/10, so method no work for every decimal.
z-m-13-07.s.s3.model.1: 0.3=3/10. 7.2÷3=2.4 but 7.2×0.3=2.16, so no same. E work only when decimal equals fraction with numerator 1, like 1/4 and 1/5.

z-m-13-02.title: Rule to change fractions to decimals for calculation: how far e okay?
z-m-13-02.topic: Calculations mixing fractions and decimals: when e okay to turn fractions into decimals
z-m-13-02.goal: Judge, changing your confidence as new data show, which fractions the change-to-decimal rule give exactly and which e give approximately, then write condition as note wey younger sibling fit read.
z-m-13-02.material: Seoha talk, 'Wen you calculate with fractions and decimals together, e easy to change all fractions to decimals. You fit just write 1/3 as 0.33.' Dem go show calculation results one by one to check how Seoha rule work. (1/3 read as 'one third' and 5/6 as 'five sixths'.)
z-m-13-02.thinking.0: Change judgment and confidence as evidence increase
z-m-13-02.thinking.1: Tell exact values apart from approximate values
z-m-13-02.thinking.2: Restate general claim by adding conditions
z-m-13-02.prereq.0: Write fractions as decimals (Grade 5 level, like 1/4 = 0.25)
z-m-13-02.s.s1.prompt: Calculation results dey show one by one. Each time choose how you view Seoha rule.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.hint.0: At each step, write result calculated with decimals and result calculated with fractions side by side, then mark where dem same and where dem differ.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.hint.1: Compare how decimal digits end when you write 1/4 and 1/3 (whether digits stop or continue forever).
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.0.info: First calculation na 1/4 + 0.5. Seoha change 1/4 = 0.25 and get 0.25 + 0.5 = 0.75. With fractions, 1/4 + 1/2 = 3/4, and 3/4 na 0.75.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.0.after: Getting same answer no mean say e be so for all fractions. 1/4 na fraction wey come out exactly as 0.25. Testing other fractions na correct next step.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Calculation results same, so answer same for any fraction.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You go from one example all the way to 'any fraction'. Think whether some fractions like 1/3 look different wen you change them to decimals.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.0.o.b: One example alone no tell us. Test other fractions too.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Na good judgment. One example being correct different from 'always correct', so you need test more.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Seoha rule wrong. If you change fraction to decimal, value change.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Even wen 1/4 change to 0.25, value no change. Work out whether some fractions' values change when you write them as decimals.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.0.o.d: Calculations mixing fractions and decimals no fit do either way.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.0.r.d: You fit calculate by making them same type, fraction with fraction or decimal with decimal. For this example both methods fit.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.1.info: Second calculation na 1/3 + 0.5. Seoha change 1/3 = 0.33 and get 0.33 + 0.5 = 0.83. With fractions, 1/3 + 1/2 = 5/6, and 5/6 as decimal na 0.8333… (the 3s continue forever).
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.1.ask: How we suppose understand Seoha answer 0.83?
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.1.after: If you round 0.8333… to second decimal place, e become 0.83. So if problem ask 'up to second decimal place', Seoha answer fit accepted. But exact value na 5/6, and 0.83 na approximate value wey small pass am. First check what accuracy the problem need.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.1.o.a: 5/6 no be 0.83, so Seoha answer wrong every time.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.1.r.a: True say 5/6 different from 0.83, but if problem ask 'up to second decimal place', 0.83 fit be answer.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.1.o.b: 0.83 and 0.8333… exactly the same number, so no need tell them apart.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.1.r.b: 0.8333… na number where 3s dey continue forever, so e small bigger than 0.83. Dem no be same number.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.1.o.c: As exact values dem different, but if na up to second decimal place, 0.83 okay too.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You separate exact values from approximate values and see say e depend on accuracy wey problem ask for.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.1.o.d: Seoha change am to 0.33, na the problem, so 0.33 + 0.5 no fit calculate.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.1.r.d: You fit calculate 0.33 + 0.5. Problem na say 1/3 value wey dem change to 0.33 no be exact.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.2.info: Third calculation na adding 1/3 three times. Seoha get 0.33 + 0.33 + 0.33 = 0.99. With fractions, 1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3 = 1.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.2.after: Small difference wey happen wen dem write 1/3 as 0.33 grow to 0.01 after dem add am three times. The more you continue calculating, the more difference fit build up, so if you need exact value, e safer to calculate with fractions as dem be.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.2.o.a: 0.99 and 1 almost same, so Seoha rule fine everywhere.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.2.r.a: The words 'almost same' no talk how close e must be. For problem wey need exact value, 0.99 no be 1.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.2.o.b: 1/3 no fit write as decimal, so no mix fractions and decimals.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.2.r.b: You fit write 1/3 as decimal where 3s dey continue forever. Mixing fractions and decimals no forbidden by itself.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Seoha rule never correct so far.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.2.r.c: For 1/4 + 0.5, Seoha method give exact value too.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Small errors dey pile up, so if you need exact value, calculate with fractions.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.st.2.r.d: You see how small errors pile up through addition and multiplication.
z-m-13-02.s.s1.reflect: Did Seoha rule seem right at first? As examples added, what changed/stayed? How tell exact value needed versus approximation enough?
z-m-13-02.s.s2.prompt: Write short note to younger sibling explaining Seoha method using fraction examples: when okay, when careful.
z-m-13-02.s.s2.hint.0: Can decimal looks of 1/4 and 1/3 serve as evidence? 1 4 1 3 1 4 1 3
z-m-13-02.s.s2.hint.1: Write two parts: 'Okay when...' and 'Careful when...'.
z-m-13-02.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Note says both when okay and when careful?
z-m-13-02.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You separate exact-value cases from cases where approximate okay?
z-m-13-02.s.s2.model.0: Fraction like 1/4 or 1/5 has exact decimal, so decimal calculation stays exact. But 1/3=0.333... repeats forever; writing 0.33 is estimate. For exact answer, calculate fractions. 1 4 1 5 1 3 0.333 0.33 1 4 1 5 1 3 0.333 0.33
z-m-13-02.s.s2.model.1: If problem only asks hundredths place, 1/3=0.33 okay. But add 0.33 three times gives 0.99, not 1, so repeated calculations pile up errors. 1 3 0.33 0.33 0.99 1 1 3 0.33 0.33 0.99 1

z-m-13-05.title: Splitting before division: which way works?
z-m-13-05.topic: Dividing mixed numbers: can you split either number before calculating?
z-m-13-05.goal: Compare two ways of splitting mixed numbers for division, using table evidence; separate what examples show from what they don't; explain why one method works and other doesn't.
z-m-13-05.material:
Gaon and Narae describe methods for dividing mixed numbers.
Gaon: 'Split the dividend into whole and fraction parts, divide each by divisor, then add.'
Narae: 'Split divisor into whole and fraction parts, divide dividend by each, then add.'
Here are their results for two problems. (2 1/2 is read 'two and one half'; 12 1/2 is 'twelve and one half.')
Problem / exact / Gaon / Narae
2 1/2 ÷ 1 1/4 / 2 / 2 / 12 1/2
3 1/3 ÷ 1 2/3 / 2 / 2 / 8 1/3
Exact answers came from converting both mixed numbers to improper fractions. 2 1 2 12 1 2 2 1 2 1 1 4 2 2 12 1 2 3 1 3 1 2 3 2 2 8 1 3
z-m-13-05.thinking.1: Distinguishing the strength of a counterexample from limits of examples
z-m-13-05.prereq.0: Writing mixed numbers as improper fractions; fraction division (Grade 6) 6
z-m-13-05.prereq.1: Case where sum of quotients equals quotient of sum (e.g. 6÷3+3÷3=9÷3) 6 3 3 3 9 3
z-m-13-05.s.s1.prompt: Choose everything you can support with table evidence.
z-m-13-05.s.s1.hint.0: Compare exact-value column with each method; mark matches and differences.
z-m-13-05.s.s1.hint.1: For each option, tell whether it reports table observation or a broader conclusion.
z-m-13-05.s.s1.o.a: Narae wrong in both, so never right for any mixed number
z-m-13-05.s.s1.r.a: Two examples only disprove 'always works'; cannot say never right without more cases.
z-m-13-05.s.s1.o.b: Gaon right twice, but not enough to know all mixed numbers.
z-m-13-05.s.s1.r.b: Correct examples don't prove always. You notice difference.
z-m-13-05.s.s1.o.c: Both methods split, divide, add, so same method
z-m-13-05.s.s1.r.c: What gets split differs: Gaon splits dividend, Narae divisor.
z-m-13-05.s.s1.o.d: Narae wrong twice, so 'always works' false.
z-m-13-05.s.s1.o.e: Gaon right twice, so works for all mixed numbers
z-m-13-05.s.s1.r.e: Several right examples don't prove all; need reason.
z-m-13-05.s.s1.explain: Narae differs from exact 2 in both, disproving always; table can't confirm never works. Gaon right twice, but examples don't prove all. Need derive reason. 2 2
z-m-13-05.s.s2.prompt: What extra evidence beyond two examples needed to say Gaon works for all mixed numbers?
z-m-13-05.s.s2.hint.1: Compare keeping divisor and splitting only dividend versus splitting divisor.
z-m-13-05.s.s2.o.a: Make some more examples with bigger numbers and count whether Gaon method correct.
z-m-13-05.s.s2.r.a: Even with more examples, we still no confirm 'all'. Examples only make your belief stronger.
z-m-13-05.s.s2.o.b: Narae method wrong, so Gaon method must correct.
z-m-13-05.s.s2.r.b: One method wrong no make the other right. You must work out Gaon method separately.
z-m-13-05.s.s2.o.c: Work out why sum of quotients from split parts equal quotient of whole number.
z-m-13-05.s.s2.o.d: Ask teacher whether Gaon method correct.
z-m-13-05.s.s2.r.d: E fit be confirmed, but e different from working out why yourself.
z-m-13-05.s.s2.explain: If you split dividend and add each part's quotient after dividing by same number, answer equal quotient when you divide whole number from start. Example: 6 ÷ 3 + 3 ÷ 3 = 9 ÷ 3. Reason same whether divisor mixed number or no, so Gaon method works every time. But if you split divisor, this reason no hold.
z-m-13-05.s.s3.prompt: Use table numbers at least once to explain why Narae method no correct.
z-m-13-05.s.s3.hint.0: Write Narae method result and exact result side by side in table; compare which bigger and by how much.
z-m-13-05.s.s3.hint.1: Check how each quotient Narae add compare with exact value.
z-m-13-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You compare using numbers from table?
z-m-13-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You explain with your own words why splitting divisor make answer too big?
z-m-13-05.s.s3.model.0: With Narae method, 2 1/2 ÷ 1 1/4 become 12 1/2, but correct answer na 2. If you split divisor into 1 and 1/4, then add results from dividing by each, quotient become too big.
z-m-13-05.s.s3.model.1: For 3 1/3 ÷ 1 2/3, Narae method give 8 1/3 but correct value na 2. Divide separately by 1 and 2/3; each quotient already big, so adding dem no correct.
